alerts.title: Los Angeles City Council Approves Sweeping Zoning Reform Package for Transit Corridors
alerts.summary: The LA City Council voted 12-3 to approve a comprehensive rezoning package that would allow denser housing along major transit corridors. The measure affects neighborhoods near Metro stations and bus rapid transit lines, permitting buildings up to 8 stories in previously single-family zones.

alerts.title: New Rent Stabilization Ordinance Expands Protections to Buildings Built Before 2005
alerts.summary: Los Angeles has expanded its Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) to cover buildings constructed before 2005, up from the previous 1978 cutoff. The change is expected to bring approximately 200,000 additional units under rent control protections.

alerts.title: Measure ULA Revenue Falls Short of Projections as Luxury Sales Slow
alerts.summary: Revenue from Los Angeles's Measure ULA transfer tax has generated $380 million in its latest fiscal year, falling roughly 25% below initial forecasts. City officials attribute the shortfall to a slowdown in high-end property transactions.

alerts.title: LAHD Issues New Guidelines for Tenant Relocation Assistance Payments
alerts.summary: The Los Angeles Housing Department has updated its relocation assistance requirements, increasing minimum payments to $12,500 for qualifying tenants. The new guidelines take effect October 1 and apply to no-fault evictions in RSO-covered buildings.

alerts.title: Planning Commission Approves 450-Unit Mixed-Use Development in Koreatown
alerts.summary: The LA Planning Commission has greenlit a major mixed-use project at Wilshire and Vermont, featuring 450 residential units, 30,000 sq ft of retail, and 15% affordable housing. The project required a zone change from C2 to C2-2D.

alerts.title: Short-Term Rental Crackdown: City Shuts Down 1,200 Illegal Airbnb Listings
alerts.summary: Los Angeles enforcement officials have removed 1,200 illegal short-term rental listings, primarily in Venice, Hollywood, and Silver Lake. Property owners face fines of up to $2,000 per day for non-compliant STR operations.

alerts.title: LADBS Fast-Tracks Seismic Retrofit Compliance for Soft-Story Buildings
alerts.summary: The LA Department of Building and Safety has announced an accelerated timeline for soft-story building retrofits, cutting the compliance deadline from 7 years to 4. Approximately 13,500 buildings are affected citywide.

alerts.title: New ADU Ordinance Allows Up to Four Units Per Single-Family Lot
alerts.summary: Under the updated Accessory Dwelling Unit ordinance, Los Angeles homeowners can now build up to four ADUs on single-family lots zoned R1, provided minimum lot size and setback requirements are met. The move is expected to add 50,000 potential housing units.

alerts.title: California Governor Signs SB 9 Expansion Eliminating More Single-Family Zoning Restrictions
alerts.summary: Governor Newsom has signed an expanded version of SB 9 that removes additional barriers to lot splitting and duplex construction on single-family parcels throughout California. The bill specifically targets HOA restrictions that had blocked many SB 9 projects.

alerts.title: Eviction Moratorium Extension Debated as Council Members Split on Tenant Protections
alerts.summary: A heated debate erupted at City Hall over whether to extend modified eviction protections that were set to expire in October. Tenant advocates argue the protections are still necessary, while landlord groups say they discourage rental investment.

alerts.title: Judge Rules Against City in Measure ULA Legal Challenge, Tax Collection Continues
alerts.summary: A Los Angeles Superior Court judge dismissed a legal challenge to Measure ULA, ruling that the transfer tax does not violate Proposition 13. The ruling clears the way for continued collection of the 4% tax on properties sold for over $5 million.

alerts.title: LA County Board of Supervisors Approves New Affordable Housing Incentive Program
alerts.summary: The Board of Supervisors unanimously approved a $500 million incentive program for affordable housing development in unincorporated LA County areas. Developers can receive up to $75,000 per unit in subsidies for projects with 50% or more affordable units.

alerts.title: Hollywood Community Plan Update Moves Forward with Increased Height Limits
alerts.summary: The long-awaited Hollywood Community Plan update has advanced to the City Council with proposals to increase building height limits along Sunset and Hollywood Boulevards from 6 to 15 stories, aiming to accommodate 35,000 new housing units by 2040.

alerts.title: HCIDLA Launches Online Portal for RSO Registration and Annual Billing
alerts.summary: The Housing + Community Investment Department has launched a new digital portal allowing landlords to register RSO units and pay annual fees online. The system replaces paper-based processes and aims to improve compliance tracking.

alerts.title: Fire Rebuild Permits Streamlined: LADBS Cuts Review Time for Palisades Reconstruction
alerts.summary: LADBS has implemented an expedited permit review process for properties destroyed in the January Palisades fire. Building permits for reconstruction will now be reviewed within 15 business days, down from the typical 45-60 day timeline.

alerts.title: AB 2011 Projects Begin Breaking Ground Along Commercial Corridors in LA
alerts.summary: The first wave of housing projects approved under California's AB 2011, which allows ministerial approval of affordable housing on commercially zoned land, have begun construction in Echo Park and North Hollywood. Combined, they will add 380 new units.

alerts.title: Tenant Groups File Lawsuit Over Just-Cause Eviction Loopholes in Owner-Move-In Cases
alerts.summary: Coalition of tenant advocacy groups has filed a class-action lawsuit alleging that landlords are abusing the owner-move-in provision of LA's just-cause eviction ordinance to illegally displace tenants. The suit claims at least 3,000 tenants have been improperly evicted.

alerts.title: City Council Proposes Transfer Tax Exemption for First-Time Homebuyers Under $750K
alerts.summary: A new City Council motion proposes exempting first-time homebuyers from LA's documentary transfer tax on properties sold below $750,000. The exemption could save qualifying buyers up to $3,375 and is aimed at improving homeownership accessibility.
